source.text: Phoebe parens, seu te Lyciae Patarea nivosis exercent dumeta iugis, seu rore pudico Castaliae flavos amor est tibi mergere crines, seu Troiam Thymbraeus habes, ubi fama volentem ingratis Phrygios umeris subiisse molares, seu iuvat Aegaeum feriens Latonius umbra Cynthus et assiduam pelago non quaerere Delon:
source.text_original: Phoebe parens, seu te Lyciae Patarea nivosis / exercent dumeta iugis, seu rore pudico / Castaliae flavos amor est tibi mergere crines, / seu Troiam Thymbraeus habes, ubi fama volentem / ingratis Phrygios umeris subiisse molares, / seu iuvat Aegaeum feriens Latonius umbra / Cynthus et assiduam pelago non quaerere Delon: /
source.text_english: Phoebe, mother, whether the snowy thickets of Lycian Patarea delight you on the ridges, or whether you take pleasure in wetting your golden hair with the chaste dew of Castalia, or whether Thymbraeus has you in Troy, where rumor says you willingly took the Phrygian harness on your unwilling shoulders, or whether Latonius Cynthus delights you, striking the Aegean with its shade, and not seeking Delos, always on the sea:

reuse.author: val
reuse.text: Protinus Inachiis ultro Tirynthius Argis advolat, Arcadio cuius flammata veneno tela puer facilesque umeris gaudentibus arcus gestat Hylas: velit ille quidem, sed dextera nondum par oneri clavaeque capax.
reuse.text_original: Protinus Inachiis ultro Tirynthius Argis / advolat, Arcadio cuius flammata veneno / tela puer facilesque umeris gaudentibus arcus / gestat Hylas: velit ille quidem, sed dextera nondum / par oneri clavaeque capax.
reuse.text_english: Straightway the Tirynthian flies of his own accord to Argos of Inachus, where Hylas carries for him the poisoned darts and the bows that delight his eager shoulders—Arcadian weapons: he would indeed wish it, but his right hand is not yet equal to the burden, nor able to bear the club.
